title: A blood-feeding visitor
hook: Compare the effects on both participants.

knows: Ecological interactions can affect participants differently.
doesNotKnow: The tick benefits and the host is harmed, a parasitic interaction. This sign convention describes the stated pair, not all effects on the ecosystem.

misconception: An interaction must affect both participants in the same way.
objective: Classify the stated effects of an ecological interaction.

claims.text: Question, diagram and reveal: A tick feeds on a host's blood and benefits while harming that host. Using + for benefit, − for harm and 0 for no appreciable effect, which signs describe Tick and Host, in that order? Tick: +; Host: −. The tick benefits and the host is harmed, a parasitic interaction. This sign convention describes the stated pair, not all effects on the ecosystem.
claims.source: Stipulated simplified example; ecological definitions: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-6-community-ecology

claims.text: Icons and signs summarize the stipulated interaction and do not quantify fitness or capture every ecological effect.

Recall: What term describes the Tick–Host interaction as stated in the lesson? The tick benefits and the host is harmed, a parasitic interaction. This sign convention describes the stated pair, not all effects on the ecosystem.
